I scaled these data by mean normalization (divided by the range), so that all variables had a mean of 0 and range of [-1, 1]. In clustering, dividing by the range (scaling) is preferable to dividing by the standard deviation (normalization) to preserve possible cluster structure in the data (Mirkin, 2016).

```{r}
#| label: "scale data"

# for each dataset:
ses_data_list_sc <- lapply(ses_data_list, function(df) {
  df %>%
    # omit rows with NAs (should be none)
    na.omit() %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    # mean normalization
    mutate(across(!c(county, year),
                  ~ (.x - mean(.x)) / (max(.x) - min(.x))))
})
```

Before clustering begins, it is useful to select the most important variables for clustering. The `clustvarsel` package uses methods to select the most optimal subset of variables that contain cluster information and suggest variables that provide little extra information to drop. It's important to note that these are locally optimal -- depending on where in parameter space the algorithm randomly starts, it is possible that different variables may be selected. To account for this, I ran the variable selection algorithm 20 times and used the list of variables most frequently selected between the 20 runs. In the end, I'm not sure if this was necessary, since every run selected the same variables.

I chose the most conservative method. The algorithm starts with all the variables, and tests dropping different variables from the equation to see if the difference is minimal.

I tested for a range of 1-5 possible clusters. It's recommended to vary the number of possible clusters between 1 and the next integer after $n^{0.3}$ (Biernacki et al., 2006).

```{r}
#| label: "variable selection bootstrap"
#| eval: false

# for each scaled dataset:
ses_var_sel <- mapply(function(df, ses_system) {
  # create a data.frame to hold results of each data selection run
  selected_vars <- data.frame(run = 1:20)
  # add variable names as column names and fill with NA values to start
  selected_vars[,colnames(df)[-c(1:2)]] <- NA
  
  # for the 20 variable selection runs
  for (i in 1:20) {
    varsel <- clustvarsel(data = df[,-c(1:2)],
              G = 1:5,
              search = "greedy",
              direction = "backward",
              fit = FALSE)
    # record if each variable name was included in the varsel result
    newrow <- (colnames(df)[-c(1:2)] %in% names(varsel$subset))
    # fill selected_vars data.frame with T/F values based on if variable was selected
    selected_vars[i,2:ncol(selected_vars)] <- newrow
  }
  # save results for each dataset
  write.csv(selected_vars,
            paste0("../data/bootstrap/", ses_system, "_var_sel.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
}, df = ses_data_list_sc, ses_system = names(ses_data_list_sc))
```

```{r}
#| label: "variable selection"

# filter out unselected variables
# for each dataset:
ses_data_sel <- mapply(function(df, ses_system) {
  # find the correct variable selection results
  file.name <- list.files(full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE,
                          pattern = "var_sel.csv",
                          path = "..")
  # read in variable selection results
  selected_vars <- read.csv(file.name[str_detect(file.name, ses_system)])
  # make sure the same variables were selected every time, otherwise stop and throw warning
  if(nrow(unique(selected_vars[,-1])) == 1) {
    varsel <- unique(selected_vars[,-1])
  } else { stop("Multiple variable selection possibilities") }
  
  # return the dataset with only the selected columns, as well as county and year
  return(df[,c(TRUE, TRUE, as.logical(varsel))])
}, df=ses_data_list_sc, 
ses_system = names(ses_data_list_sc),
SIMPLIFY = FALSE)
```

### Gaussian Model-Based Clustering

To select a model, which includes selecting the number of groups and the shape, I used BIC to test 14 different model shapes and 1-5 possible clusters. It's recommended to vary the number of possible clusters between 1 and the next integer after $n^{0.3}$ (Biernacki et al., 2006).

Since this clustering finds local maxima, it is sensitive to its initialization. I ran the cluster models 200 times for each SES subsystem, preserving the best model as the final result.

```{r}
#| label: "model selection"

ses_mclustBIC <- lapply(ses_data_sel, function(df) {
  BIC <- NULL
  LL <- NULL
  for(j in 1:200) {
    rBIC <- mclustBIC(df[,-c(1:2)], G=1:5, verbose=FALSE,
                    initalization = list(hcPairs=hcRandomPairs(df[,-c(1:2)])))
    rModel <- mclustModel(df[,-c(1:2)], BICvalues = rBIC)
    LL <- c(LL, rModel$loglik)
    BIC <- mclustBICupdate(BIC, rBIC)
  }
  list(mod=Mclust(df[,-c(1:2)], x = BIC), LL=LL)
})
```

<!-- for hist code, see https://centerstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/CAMM-mixture-modeling-demo-R-2021.pdf page 5-19 -->

`r ses_mclustBIC[["Resource"]]$mod$G` clusters was the best fit for the resource data. `r ses_mclustBIC[["Actors"]]$mod$G` clusters was the best fit for the resource data.

To get a sense for how the data are clustering, we can view their groups on a principal components graph.

```{r}
pca_viz <- lapply(ses_data_sel, function(df) {
  prcomp(df[,-c(1:2)])
})

factoextra::fviz_pca_biplot(
  pca_viz[["Resource"]],
  habillage=as.factor(ses_mclustBIC[["Resource"]]$mod$classification),
  title = "Resource",
  geom = "point", repel = TRUE,
  addEllipses = TRUE)
factoextra::fviz_pca_biplot(
  pca_viz[["Actors"]],
  habillage=as.factor(ses_mclustBIC[["Actors"]]$mod$classification),
  title = "Actors",
  geom = "point", repel = TRUE,
  addEllipses = TRUE)
```

The mclust package also has built-in methods for principle component analysis of clusters:

```{r}
# run dimension reduction for both models
drmod_resource <- MclustDR(ses_mclustBIC$Resource$mod)
drmod_actors <- MclustDR(ses_mclustBIC$Actors$mod)

# view DR summary
summary(drmod_resource)

########### method to find influential terms

# general code
# get cumulative influence of each dimension
mults <- c(summary(drmod_actors)$evalues.cumperc[1], (summary(drmod_actors)$evalues.cumperc - lag(summary(drmod_actors)$evalues.cumperc))[2:length(summary(drmod_actors)$evalues.cumperc)]) / 100

# total contribution of each variable = sum of its contributions to each variable weighted by overall contribution of each dimension
# absolute value is used to equally weight negative and positive contribution to dimensions
row_vals <- apply(summary(drmod_actors)$basis, 1, 
                     function(row) {
                       row_val <- sum(abs(row * mults))
                     })
# add variable names to contributions
names(row_vals) <- row.names(summary(drmod_actors)$basis)
# view results
print(row_vals[order(row_vals, decreasing=TRUE)])

# influence - resources
mults <- c(summary(drmod_resource)$evalues.cumperc[1], (summary(drmod_resource)$evalues.cumperc - lag(summary(drmod_resource)$evalues.cumperc))[2:length(summary(drmod_resource)$evalues.cumperc)]) / 100

row_vals <- apply(summary(drmod_resource)$basis, 1, 
                     function(row) {
                       row_val <- sum(abs(row * mults))
                     })
names(row_vals) <- row.names(summary(drmod_resource)$basis)
# save results
write.csv(data.frame(indicator = names(row_vals)[order(row_vals, decreasing=TRUE)],
                     influence = row_vals[order(row_vals, decreasing=TRUE)]),
          "../data/model results/drmod_resource.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)

# influence - actors
mults <- c(summary(drmod_actors)$evalues.cumperc[1], (summary(drmod_actors)$evalues.cumperc - lag(summary(drmod_actors)$evalues.cumperc))[2:length(summary(drmod_actors)$evalues.cumperc)]) / 100

row_vals <- apply(summary(drmod_actors)$basis, 1, 
                     function(row) {
                       row_val <- sum(abs(row * mults))
                     })
names(row_vals) <- row.names(summary(drmod_actors)$basis)
# save results
write.csv(data.frame(indicator = names(row_vals)[order(row_vals, decreasing=TRUE)],
                     influence = row_vals[order(row_vals, decreasing=TRUE)]),
          "../data/model results/drmod_actors.csv", 
          row.names = FALSE)
```


```{r}
#| label: "get CIs"
#| include: false

# for each cluster model, get confidence intervals for each variable:
ci_clust <- mapply(function(mod, ses_system, input_data) {
  # use bootstrapping to get CIs
  bootmod <- MclustBootstrap(mod$mod, nboot = 999, type = "wlbs")
  
  # get mean value for each variable in each cluster
  clust_means <- as.data.frame(mod$mod$parameters$mean) %>%
    # convert variable names to a proper column instead of row names
    mutate(input_data_name = rownames(.)) %>%
    # convert to tidy format
    pivot_longer(cols = !input_data_name,
                 names_to = "cluster",
                 values_to = "mean") %>%
    # label with resource or actors model and cluster number
    mutate(cluster = str_replace(cluster, "V", substr(ses_system,1,1)))
  
  # get the CI lower and upper limits
  t(as.data.frame(summary(bootmod, "ci")$mean)) %>%
    as.data.frame() %>%
    # label clusters and variables properly
    mutate(cluster = paste0(str_sub(ses_system, 1,1), str_sub(rownames(.), -1, -1)),
           input_data_name = str_sub(rownames(.), 1, -3),
           # assign significance based on if CI contains 0
           sig = !(`2.5%`<0 & `97.5%`>0)) %>%
    # join on variable means
    left_join(clust_means, by = c("input_data_name", "cluster"))
}, mod = ses_mclustBIC, ses_system = names(ses_data_sel), input_data = ses_data_sel, SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

# save results
write.csv(ci_clust[["Resource"]], "../data/model results/ci_clust_resource.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(ci_clust[["Actors"]], "../data/model results/ci_clust_actors.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# add cluster numbers to scaled data
clust_dat_sc <- mapply(function(df, mod, system_name) {
  left_join(df, aoi[,c("NAME", "geometry")], by = c("county" = "NAME")) %>%
    st_as_sf() %>%
    cbind(., mod$mod$classification) %>%
    mutate(cluster = paste0(substr(system_name,1,1), mod.mod.classification)) %>%
    select(-mod.mod.classification)
}, df = ses_data_list_sc, mod = ses_mclustBIC, system_name=names(ses_data_list))

# save results
write.csv(st_drop_geometry(clust_dat_sc[["Resource"]]),
          "../data/model results/clust_dat_sc_resource.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(st_drop_geometry(clust_dat_sc[["Actors"]]),
          "../data/model results/clust_dat_sc_actors.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
          "../data/model results/clust_dat_actors.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)

# tables of mean, min, and max values for each variable in each cluster (not used)
resource_means <- clust_dat$Resource %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE))

actor_means <- clust_dat$Actors %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE))
```
